Companies' Complementary Portfolios, Shared Vision and Values Are Key Drivers for Acquisition
NEW YORK, March 4, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Panebianco Wines (www.panebiancowines.com), a premier and boutique importer and distributor of fine Italian wines, announces the acquisition of DB Wine Selections (www.dbwineselection.com), a distinguished purveyor of high-quality French wines. This strategic acquisition strengthens Panebianco Wines' position as a leader in fine wine importation and distribution, broadening its reach across the Northeast while maintaining the integrity and legacy of both storied companies.  The acquisition gives Panebianco a strong portfolio of suppliers from the two leading regions of imported wine in the US: Italy (by volume) and France (by value).
Under the terms of the acquisition, DB Wine Selections will continue to operate under its existing name with its president, Didier Boutet, remaining in his role to lead the integration process and drive the business into the future. This move ensures continuity for DB Wine Selections' clientele, suppliers and team members while facilitating a seamless transition and expansion for both organizations and portfolios.
"This acquisition represents a milestone for both Panebianco Wines and DB Wine Selections," said Nunzio Castaldo, President of Panebianco Wines. "Panebianco's deep-rooted expertise in Italian wines and DB Wine Selections' esteemed reputation for curating exceptional French wines allows each of us to expand our portfolio offerings for our respective client bases, leverage our shared passion for fine wines, and enhance our service capabilities across key markets. We're excited to bring together two companies that share a dedication to estate wines of quality, authenticity, and craftsmanship."
For over 27 years, Panebianco Wines has been a trusted name, working with top estate, family-owned producers to bring the finest selection of Italian wines to American wine lovers. Similarly, DB Wine Selections has cultivated an unparalleled reputation for curating high-caliber French wines, making it a natural complement to Panebianco Wines' growing portfolio. The acquisition will allow both companies to maintain their brand identities while creating new opportunities for employee growth, supplier partnerships, and customer engagement.
"Our goal is to expand our presence in the Northeast while staying true to the heritage and specialization that make Panebianco and DB Wine Selections leaders in their respective categories," said Didier Boutet. "Together, we'll continue to elevate the wine experience for sommeliers, beverage directors and fine wine buyers – and ultimately American wine lovers -- bringing an even more robust selection of fine wines to the market.  And we will build the leading team of French and Italian wine experts in the entire Northeast!"
"This acquisition reflects Panebianco Wines' ongoing commitment to excellence, innovation, and expansion in the fine wine industry," continued Castaldo. "Customers, team members and partners can expect the same high standards of service and product selection as the company continues to grow."

About
6BB1C530-68DC-41B7-AE7F-6B02052B9867_edited.png
French Wine Importer and wholesaler
OUR WINE PRODUCERS
Our portfolio brings together a curated selection of wineries across the South of France, including Provence, Languedoc-Roussillon and the Rhône Valley.
​
We work directly with producers who combine strong identity, consistent quality and clear commercial positioning, from accessible entry-level wines to premium cuvées.
​
Through our close relationships and on-the-ground presence, we offer partners access to reliable supply, competitive pricing and wines adapted to international markets.
​
Each winery is selected not only for quality, but for its ability to perform in export markets.
Domaine de la Croix.jpg
Domaine de La Croix is the largest “Cru Classé” vineyard in Provence. It produces high-quality Côtes de Provence Cru Classé wines raised in the soils of the Saint-Tropez peninsula. The property covers 445 acres, including 150 acres of vines, facing the Mediterranean Sea from Gassin to Ramatuelle. Established in 1882, the domain was purchased by The Bolloré group in 2001 and has since been restructured to recover the excellence of its terroir. Using traditional methods for sustainable wine growing, attracting great names like renowned winemaker Michel Rolland, Domaine de La Croix is nowadays recognized for its uniqueness and for the exceptional quality of its wines.
Vignerons Associés des Monts de Bourgogne.jpg
The Union des Vignerons Associés des Monts de Bourgogne was founded in 2015 when winegrowers from Côte d’Or and Mconnais united around shared values. With expertise in expressing the nuances of Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Gamay, and Aligoté, the Union is strongly committed to sustainable and cooperative winemaking. Their retail brands, Blason de Bourgogne and Monts de Bourgogne, bring together over 200 winegrowing families rooted in the vineyards stretching from Côte d’Or to Mconnais. This diversity enriches the wines with aromatic complexity and character. The Mconnais, in particular, is gaining recognition for its vibrant, accessible wines, reflecting a rising trend. These wines embody generations of tradition and viticultural know-how.
tardieu laurent.jpg
Maison Tardieu-Laurent was founded in 1994 by Michel Tardieu and Dominique Laurent in Provence. Tardieu has significantly influenced the development and evolution of Rhone wines; with no vineyard property of his own, he chooses the vineyards he likes and agrees to the conditions of viticulture and processing with each of the producers. Thus, its catalog not only includes wines from almost all denominations of Rhone wines made, but all with grapes from old vines, some of the oldest in the area. All of his wines are produced environmentally friendly and free of chemicals. Tardieu follows the philosophy of minimal intervention, without decanting filtration or cold stabilisation at the time of bottling. This helps to preserve maximum character from each terroir.
Domaine Magalone 2.jpg
Domaine Magalone is a young estate born from a passion for viticulture and a vision for organic farming. Today, it covers 10 hectares of organically farmed vines, nestled among pine and oak forests on sandy-clay-limestone soils, ideally exposed south-southeast. The estate produces wines that reflect the richness of the Provençal terroir, including Villa Magalone Premium Blanc, Villa Magalone Premium Rosé, and Everose by Magalone. Each cuvée is crafted with a commitment to sustainability, authenticity, and terroir expression. Domaine Magalone stands out for its environmentally respectful philosophy and dedication to producing organic wines that capture the spirit and elegance of southern Provence.
Cave De Tain.jpg
Joel Delaunay.jpg
On the left bank of the Rhône, the Hermitage hill dominates the Crozes-Hermitage appellation, while on the right, Saint-Joseph, Cornas, and Saint-Péray stretch across terraced slopes. Across these five vineyards and the Collines Rhodaniennes, Cave de Tain l’Hermitage offers exceptional varietal and terroir diversity. Founded in 1933, the producer has grown through generations of dedicated winegrowers to become a flagship of the northern Rhône and Europe’s top producer of appellation Syrah wines. Nowadays, the Cave works to preserve the diversity and quality of these iconic grapes. Syrah is the sole red grape behind the region’s five great red AOCs: Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage, Saint-Joseph, Cornas, and Côte-Rôtie.
The Delaunay family have been family winemakers for 5 generations.
The Estate is located near the famous Chteau de Chenonceau, east of Tours in a small village Pouillé (41). Proud of our 45 hectares in the Touraine and Touraine Chenonceaux appellations, the green lines of our family vineyard adorn the hillsides bordering the Cher river. The winery is certified as practising sustainable agriculture since 2006. Their wines have experienced a significant success in the exports markets (Waitrose, SAQ in Canada, Systembolaget in Sweden, etc) thanks to a classic but contemporary presentation and a consistent quality that has been awarded internationally (James Suckling, Wine Enthusiast, etc.)
Domaine Arnaud Aucoeur.jpg
Arnaud Aucoeur has been voted 2020 Winemaker of the Year in Beaujolais by the famous “Guide Hachette” in France. He epitomizes the Beaujolais revival over the past few years in the world of wine. Since 1825, the Domaine Aucoeur has been established in Villié Morgon with vines growing on 12 hectares of on the most prestigious crus: Morgon, Fleurie, Moulin à Vent, etc. To perpetuate its legacy, Arnaud makes some of his wines in wooden containers. The whole production is done manually, barrels, tons and semi-casks are housed on the farm, and the wines are all raised, vinified and packaged according to particular emotional and technical conditions of the domain.
Vignobles Berthier 2 (1).jpg.jpg)
Vignobles Berthier is a family-owned winery located in the heart of the Loire Valley, France. The Berthier family has been cultivating vineyards for several generations, focusing on producing high-quality wines that reflect the unique terroirs of the region. The estate spans across three prestigious appellations: Sancerre, Pouilly-Fumé, and Coteaux du Giennois. The Berthier family combines traditional winemaking techniques with modern innovations to produce wines that are both authentic and contemporary. Their commitment to quality is evident in every bottle, from the careful selection of grapes to the meticulous winemaking process.
Vignobles Chevron Villette.jpg
Vignobles Chevron Villette is a historic, family-owned estate in Provence, with roots tracing back to the 12th century. Today, it spans over 550 hectares across several chteaux, including Reillanne and Camparnaud. The estate is a pioneer in sustainable viticulture, with a strong commitment to organic and biodynamic farming since 2016. Specializing in Côtes-de-Provence rosés, along with select reds and whites, its wines are crafted through precise, plot-by-plot selection to express the character of each terroir. Blending tradition with modern practices, the estate reflects both heritage and innovation. As demand rises for authentic, eco-conscious wines, Chevron Villette stands out for its quality, sustainability, and dedication to showcasing the diversity and elegance of the Provençal landscape.
Famille Gaillard.jpg
Famille Gaillard is one of the Rhône Valley's most respected family-owned wine estates, founded by renowned winemaker Pierre Gaillard. Today, the family farms exceptional vineyards across Côte-Rôtie, Condrieu, Saint-Joseph, Crozes-Hermitage and Collines Rhodaniennes, combining meticulous vineyard management with a deep respect for terroir. Their philosophy focuses on expressing the purity and elegance of each appellation through sustainable viticulture and precise winemaking. Distributed in leading restaurants, specialist wine merchants and fine wine markets across more than 40 countries, Famille Gaillard has built an international reputation for producing authentic Rhône wines of outstanding quality, finesse and consistency.
